failure_class.name: GitHub-hosted Actions jobs fail before runner allocation
failure_class.hypothesis: The shared failure is upstream of repository workflow steps because it reproduces across three private repositories and two hosted runner labels with runner_id=0, empty runner_name and zero steps. Repository code/test failures are therefore not evidenced by these runs.

external_evidence: GitHub Community #207926 (2026-09-15): hosted jobs across private repos fail before allocation with runner_id=0, empty runner_name and steps=[]
GitHub Community #208438 (2026-09-21): identical pre-runner failure signature in a private repository
GitHub Community #207125 (2026-09-08): zero-step/no-runner hosted failures; guidance classifies job-with-empty-steps as runner provisioning before checkout
internal_alternatives_considered: Change workflow commands/dependencies: REJECTED; no step starts
Switch ubuntu-latest to ubuntu-24.04: REJECTED as general fix; video already fails identically on ubuntu-24.04
Treat failed hosted CI as code regression evidence: REJECTED
Disable hosted CI requirement: REJECTED; would reduce assurance rather than fix the failure

disposition.reason: Current evidence points to an external host/account admission or runner-provisioning layer. Adding repository mechanisms would be speculative complexity and violates anti-bloat/root-cause governance.
next_actions: Check GitHub account/repository Actions policy, usage/billing and hosted-runner eligibility through an admin-capable surface; current connector cannot read that endpoint.
Preserve run/job IDs and UTC timestamps for GitHub Support if account settings do not explain the failure.
Re-run hosted CI after the external condition changes; only a job with actual runner allocation/steps can provide hosted test evidence.
